controls.discussion: An information security architecture is a representation of the overall organizational security posture. The security architecture reflects how selected security controls and control enhancements are implemented within the overall organizational information security posture.

controls.title: Central Management
controls.statement: Centrally manage [Assignment: organization-defined controls and related processes].
controls.discussion: Many security controls are allocated to both organizational programs and individual systems as part of the risk management process. Organizations benefit from centrally managing those controls that are not system-specific. Central management of controls reduces the cost and complexity of system-level implementations.

controls.title: Baseline Selection
controls.statement: Select a control baseline for the system.
controls.discussion: Organizations use risk assessments, information from previous assessments, and threat intelligence to select appropriate baselines for their systems. Baseline selection considers the organization's risk tolerance, applicable policies and guidance, the capabilities of the system, and the threats the system will face.

controls.title: Baseline Tailoring
controls.statement: Tailor the selected control baseline by applying specified tailoring actions.
controls.discussion: Tailoring of baselines involves applying designated tailoring actions to selected baseline controls to build the security plans for the system. Tailoring actions include selecting parameters, adding compensating controls, applying overlays, identifying common controls, and scoping the applicability of controls.

controls.title: Information Security Program Plan

items.label: PM-1a: Develop and disseminate an organization-wide information security program plan that: 1. Provides an overview of the requirements for the security program and a description of the security program management controls and common controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements; 2. Includes the identification and assignment of roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; 3. Reflects the coordination among organizational entities responsible for information security; and 4. Is approved by a senior official with responsibility and accountability for the risk being incurred to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, and reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation

controls.discussion: Program management controls are distinct from organizational, mission/business process-level, and information system-level controls. Program management controls describe organization-wide program management activities necessary for managing the information security program.

controls.title: Information Security Program Leadership Role
controls.objective_name: PM-2: Information Security Program Leadership Role
controls.statement: Appoint a senior agency information security officer with the mission and resources to coordinate, develop, implement, and maintain an organization-wide information security program.
controls.discussion: The senior agency information security officer (SAISO), also known as the Chief Information Security Officer, is responsible for carrying out the Chief Information Officer security responsibilities and serving as the primary liaison for the Chief Information Officer to the agency's authorizing officials, information system owners, common control providers, and information system security officers.

controls.title: Information Security and Privacy Resources
controls.objective_name: PM-3: Information Security and Privacy Resources

items.label: PM-3a: Include the resources needed to implement the information security and privacy programs in capital planning and investment requests and document all exceptions to this requirement
items.text: Include the resources needed to implement the information security and privacy programs in capital planning and investment requests and document all exceptions to this requirement

items.label: PM-3b: Prepare documentation required for addressing information security and privacy programs in capital planning and investment requests in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards; and
items.text: Prepare documentation required for addressing information security and privacy programs in capital planning and investment requests in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards; and

items.label: PM-3c: Make available for expenditure, the planned information security and privacy resources.
items.text: Make available for expenditure, the planned information security and privacy resources.

controls.discussion: The purpose of this control is to ensure that organizations have a process in place for planning and tracking the funding and resources needed to protect organizational information, information systems, and capabilities.

controls.title: Plan of Action and Milestones Process
controls.objective_name: PM-4: Plan of Action and Milestones Process

items.label: PM-4a: Implement a process to ensure that plans of action and milestones for the information security, privacy, and supply chain risk management programs and associated organizational systems: 1. Are developed and maintained; 2. Document the remedial information security, privacy, and supply chain risk management actions to adequately respond to risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation; and 3. Are reported in accordance with established reporting requirements.
items.text: Implement a process to ensure that plans of action and milestones for the information security, privacy, and supply chain risk management programs and associated organizational systems: 1. Are developed and maintained; 2. Document the remedial information security, privacy, and supply chain risk management actions to adequately respond to risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation; and 3. Are reported in accordance with established reporting requirements.

items.label: PM-4b: Review plans of action and milestones for consistency with the organizational risk management strategy and organization-wide priorities for risk response actions.
items.text: Review plans of action and milestones for consistency with the organizational risk management strategy and organization-wide priorities for risk response actions.

controls.discussion: Plan of action and milestones (POA&M) processes are used to document planned corrective actions related to identified deficiencies or weaknesses in organizational information security programs and systems, and the resources and milestones associated with corrective actions.

controls.title: System Inventory
controls.statement: Develop and update [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] an inventory of organizational systems.
controls.discussion: System inventories support the development of mission and business processes that rely on system assets, and the application of appropriate security policies. System inventories may be developed in different ways including manual or automated approaches. Organizations maintain system inventories throughout the system development life cycle.

controls.title: Measures of Performance
controls.statement: Develop, monitor, and report on the results of information security and privacy measures of performance.
controls.discussion: Measures of performance are quantitative measures that provide management with the information needed to make risk-based decisions on whether to implement security controls, and if so, how to improve them. Organizations use assessments, audits, and monitoring tools to obtain information to make performance measurement decisions.

controls.title: Enterprise Architecture
controls.statement: Develop an enterprise architecture with consideration for information security and privacy and the resulting risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.
controls.discussion: The enterprise architecture developed by the organization provides a foundation for consistent security and privacy decisions across the organization. Security and privacy considerations in the enterprise architecture help to ensure that systems are built with inherent security and privacy features.

controls.title: Critical Infrastructure Plan
controls.statement: Address information security and privacy issues in the development, documentation, and updating of a critical infrastructure and key resources protection plan.
controls.discussion: Information security requirements are embedded in the development, documentation, and updating of a critical infrastructure and key resources (CIKR) protection plan. The plan is used to address information security risks to the critical infrastructure and key resources and to guide security activities.

controls.title: Risk Management Strategy

items.label: PM-9a: Develops a comprehensive strategy to manage: 1. Security risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation associated with the operation and use of organizational systems; and 2. Privacy risk to individuals resulting from the authorized processing of personally identifiable information
items.text: Develops a comprehensive strategy to manage: 1. Security risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation associated with the operation and use of organizational systems; and 2. Privacy risk to individuals resulting from the authorized processing of personally identifiable information

items.label: PM-9b: Implement the risk management strategy consistently across the organization; and
items.text: Implement the risk management strategy consistently across the organization; and

items.text: Review and update the risk management strategy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] or as required, to address organizational changes.

controls.discussion: Organizational risk management strategy includes an expression of the security risk tolerance for the organization, security risk-related considerations for organizational acquisitions or outsourcing decisions, a process for consistently evaluating risk across the organization using a common taxonomy for assets, threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, and impact, and approaches for monitoring risk on an ongoing basis.

controls.title: Authorization Process

items.label: PM-10a: Manage the security and privacy state of organizational systems and the environments in which those systems operate through authorization processes
items.text: Manage the security and privacy state of organizational systems and the environments in which those systems operate through authorization processes

items.label: PM-10b: Designate individuals to fulfill specific roles and responsibilities within the organizational risk management process; and
items.text: Designate individuals to fulfill specific roles and responsibilities within the organizational risk management process; and

items.label: PM-10c: Integrate the authorization processes into an organization-wide risk management program.
items.text: Integrate the authorization processes into an organization-wide risk management program.

controls.discussion: Security authorization processes for organizational systems provide senior officials with the information needed to make risk-based decisions on whether to authorize systems to operate, and if so, under what conditions. Organizations use authorization processes to manage organizational risk commensurate with the risk tolerance defined by senior leaders or executives.

controls.title: Mission and Business Process Definition
controls.objective_name: PM-11: Mission and Business Process Definition

items.label: PM-11a: Define organizational mission and business processes with consideration for information security and privacy and the resulting risk to organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation; and
items.text: Define organizational mission and business processes with consideration for information security and privacy and the resulting risk to organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation; and

items.label: PM-11b: Determine information protection and personally identifiable information processing needs arising from the defined mission and business processes; and
items.text: Determine information protection and personally identifiable information processing needs arising from the defined mission and business processes; and

items.label: PM-11c: Review and revise the mission and business processes [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].
items.text: Review and revise the mission and business processes [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

controls.discussion: Mission and business process definition and management considers the alignment of security requirements with mission and business processes to ensure that the processes are adequately protected and that the information systems supporting those processes are appropriately scoped.

controls.title: Insider Threat Program
controls.statement: Implement an insider threat program that includes a cross-discipline insider threat incident handling team.
controls.discussion: Organizations with insider threat programs in place are in a better position to detect, deter, and mitigate adverse effects of insider threats. Organizations use cross-discipline teams to implement insider threat programs.

controls.title: Security and Privacy Workforce
controls.statement: Establish a security and privacy workforce development and improvement program.
controls.discussion: A security and privacy workforce development and improvement program addresses training and education for all organizational roles to ensure that personnel are adequately prepared to carry out their assigned security and privacy responsibilities.

controls.title: Testing, Training, and Monitoring

items.label: PM-14a: Implement a process for ensuring that organizational plans for conducting security and privacy testing, training, and monitoring activities associated with organizational systems: 1. Are developed and maintained; and 2. Continue to be executed; and
items.text: Implement a process for ensuring that organizational plans for conducting security and privacy testing, training, and monitoring activities associated with organizational systems: 1. Are developed and maintained; and 2. Continue to be executed; and

items.label: PM-14b: Review testing, training, and monitoring plans for consistency with the organizational risk management strategy and organization-wide priorities for risk response actions.
items.text: Review testing, training, and monitoring plans for consistency with the organizational risk management strategy and organization-wide priorities for risk response actions.

controls.discussion: Testing, training, and monitoring activities are important methods for identifying security and privacy controls that are not effective or that have become ineffective over time. These activities ensure that current practices and controls are effective in protecting organizational information and privacy.

controls.title: Security and Privacy Groups and Associations
controls.objective_name: PM-15: Security and Privacy Groups and Associations

items.label: PM-15a: To facilitate ongoing security and privacy education and training for organizational personnel
items.text: To facilitate ongoing security and privacy education and training for organizational personnel

items.text: To maintain currency with recommended security and privacy practices, techniques, and technologies; and

items.label: PM-15c: To share current security and privacy information, including threats, vulnerabilities, and incidents.
items.text: To share current security and privacy information, including threats, vulnerabilities, and incidents.

controls.discussion: Information sharing organizations and special interest groups provide access to current security and privacy threat and vulnerability information that can help organizations better protect their systems. Organizations share information with these groups as part of information exchange. Organizations also contribute their security and privacy experiences and knowledge to these groups to benefit the broader community.

controls.title: Threat Awareness Program
controls.statement: Implement a threat awareness program that includes a cross-organization information-sharing capability for threat intelligence.
controls.discussion: A threat awareness program helps ensure that all levels of the organization, including senior managers, system administrators, and users, are kept informed about current threats and vulnerabilities that could affect organizational systems and operations.

controls.title: Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information on External Systems
controls.objective_name: PM-17: Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information on External Systems

items.label: PM-17a: Establish policy and procedures to ensure that requirements for the protection of controlled unclassified information that is processed, stored or transmitted on external systems, are implemented in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, and standards; and
items.text: Establish policy and procedures to ensure that requirements for the protection of controlled unclassified information that is processed, stored or transmitted on external systems, are implemented in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, and standards; and

items.label: PM-17b: Review and update the policy and procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].
items.text: Review and update the policy and procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

controls.discussion: The security and privacy posture of systems can be affected by changes within organizations, including organizational restructuring, changes in key personnel, changes in technology, changes in mission/business processes, and changes in applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, standards, and guidelines. Organizations use defined processes to ensure that such changes are addressed in a timely manner.

controls.title: Privacy Program Plan

items.label: PM-18a: Develop and disseminate an organization-wide privacy program plan that provides an overview of the agency’s privacy program, and: 1. Includes a description of the structure of the privacy program and the resources dedicated to the privacy program; 2. Provides an overview of the requirements for the privacy program and a description of the privacy program management controls and common controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements; 3. Includes the role of the senior agency official for privacy and the identification and assignment of roles of other privacy officials and staff and their responsibilities; 4. Describes management commitment, compliance, and the strategic goals and objectives of the privacy program; 5. Reflects coordination among organizational entities responsible for the different aspects of privacy; and 6. Is approved by a senior official with responsibility and accountability for the privacy risk being incurred to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, and reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation; and
items.text: Develop and disseminate an organization-wide privacy program plan that provides an overview of the agency’s privacy program, and: 1. items.text: Update the plan [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and to address changes in federal privacy laws and policy and organizational changes and problems identified during plan implementation or privacy control assessments.

controls.discussion: Privacy program plans are a formal document that provides an overview of an organization's privacy program, including a description of the structure of the privacy program, the resources dedicated to the privacy program, the role of the senior agency official for privacy and other privacy staff, the strategic goals and objectives of the privacy program, and the program management controls and common controls in place or planned for meeting applicable privacy requirements and managing privacy risks.

controls.title: Privacy Program Leadership Role
controls.statement: Appoint a senior agency official for privacy with the authority, mission, accountability, and resources to coordinate, develop, and implement, applicable privacy requirements and manage privacy risks through the organization-wide privacy program.
controls.discussion: The senior agency official for privacy (SAOP) is the senior organizational official who has the authority, mission, accountability, and resources to ensure the organization's implementation of privacy protections and compliance with applicable privacy requirements. The SAOP works with the SAISO and other organizational officials to carry out privacy responsibilities.

controls.title: Dissemination of Privacy Program Information
controls.objective_name: PM-20: Dissemination of Privacy Program Information

items.label: PM-20a: Ensures that the public has access to information about organizational privacy activities and can communicate with its senior agency official for privacy
items.text: Ensures that the public has access to information about organizational privacy activities and can communicate with its senior agency official for privacy

items.text: Ensures that organizational privacy practices and reports are publicly available; and

items.label: PM-20c: Employs publicly facing email addresses and/or phone lines to enable the public to provide feedback and/or direct questions to privacy offices regarding privacy practices.
items.text: Employs publicly facing email addresses and/or phone lines to enable the public to provide feedback and/or direct questions to privacy offices regarding privacy practices.

controls.discussion: Organizations communicate their privacy policies and practices through privacy notices (informing individuals how and why PII is collected, used, maintained, and shared), the use of plain language, and making privacy policies and notices readily accessible.

controls.title: Accounting of Disclosures

Name and address, or other contact information of the individual or organization to which the disclosure was made

items.text: Retain the accounting of disclosures for the length of the time the personally identifiable information is maintained or five years after the disclosure is made, whichever is longer; and

controls.discussion: Organizations develop, disseminate, and update privacy policies and practices. An accountability approach to privacy enables organizations to meet privacy obligations as they arise from applicable laws, regulations, and guidance and demonstrates due care to individuals whose privacy interests are at stake.

items.text: Appeals of adverse decisions on correction or deletion requests.

controls.discussion: Data quality is essential for protecting privacy. Organizations implement safeguards to ensure that PII is accurate, relevant, timely, and complete. Organizations develop policies and procedures for data quality management and monitoring.

controls.statement: Establish [Assignment: organization-defined roles] to assume responsibility for developing and maintaining a comprehensive data governance program that includes [Assignment: organization-defined requirements].
controls.discussion: A data governance body assists organizations in managing the data lifecycle, ensuring data quality, and overseeing compliance with data-related policies and regulations. Data governance activities include defining data ownership, establishing data policies, and monitoring compliance with data standards.

items.text: Conduct an annual review of all matching programs in which the agency has participated.

controls.discussion: Data integrity boards review and approve research plans involving PII. The boards help ensure that appropriate measures are taken to protect PII when it is used for research, testing, or training purposes.

controls.discussion: Minimizing the use of PII for testing, training, and research reduces the risk of inappropriate or unauthorized access to PII and the associated privacy risks. controls.discussion: Complaint management processes provide individuals with a means to raise concerns about the organization's handling of their PII and to have those concerns addressed. Organizations respond to complaints in a timely manner and use complaint information to improve privacy practices.

controls.discussion: Organizations use privacy reporting mechanisms to demonstrate compliance with applicable privacy requirements and to communicate the results of privacy program activities to senior managers and oversight bodies. Privacy reports may address issues such as the status of privacy controls, privacy incidents, and the results of privacy impact assessments.

Organizations determine the required vulnerability scanning for all system components, ensuring that potential sources of vulnerabilities such as networked printers, scanners, and copiers are not overlooked.

controls.discussion: Technical surveillance countermeasures surveys are performed by qualified personnel to detect technical surveillance devices and hazards and to identify technical security weaknesses that could facilitate technical exploitation. Surveys provide a formal evaluation of the technical security posture of organizational facilities and are conducted by organizations or external providers with appropriate expertise and equipment.

controls.title: Risk Response
controls.statement: Respond to findings from security and privacy assessments, monitoring, and audits in accordance with organizational risk tolerance.
controls.discussion: Risk response is the process of responding to risks identified through the risk assessment process. Risk responses include accepting risk, avoiding risk, mitigating risk, sharing risk, and transferring risk. Organizations use risk response options to address organizational risk in a manner consistent with organizational risk tolerance.

controls.discussion: Privacy risk assessment is a systematic examination of privacy risks associated with the processing of PII. Organizations conduct privacy risk assessments to identify and evaluate the risks and potential harms associated with how they process PII, the likelihood that such harms will materialize, and the measures organizations can employ to mitigate those risks.

controls.title: Criticality Analysis
controls.statement: Identify and prioritize [Assignment: organization-defined systems and system components] based on which functions, ports, protocols, and services are of greatest importance to organizational mission and business functions, and which require protection from adversaries with greater capability.
controls.discussion: Not all system components present the same level of risk to the organization. Adversaries may be limited in their ability to target systems, and organizations can use this to their advantage by focusing protection on the most critical assets. Criticality analysis allows organizations to identify which system components are the most important to protect from adversaries with the greatest capabilities.

controls.title: Threat Hunting

items.text: Establish and maintain a cyber threat hunting capability to: 1. Search for indicators of compromise in organizational systems; and 2. Detect, track, and disrupt threats that evade existing controls; and

items.text: Employ the threat hunting capability [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

controls.discussion: A threat hunting capability allows organizations to proactively search for signs of compromise or threats within their environments. Unlike traditional intrusion detection systems that are passive, threat hunting is an active process that involves hypothesis-driven investigations into potential threats.

Organizations develop their own SDLCs or use industry SDLCs. Security and privacy are integrated into the SDLC through the identification and implementation of security controls throughout the development phases.

Organizations apply the engineering principles throughout the system development life cycle, including security and privacy considerations in the requirements, design, development, test, deployment, and maintenance phases.

items.text: Require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to follow a documented development process that: 1. Explicitly addresses security and privacy requirements; 2. Development processes provide organizations with increased visibility into the security posture of systems under development and allow organizations to identify and address potential security and privacy issues before they manifest in the operational environment.

controls.statement: Require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to provide [Assignment: organization-defined training] on the correct use and operation of the implemented security and privacy functions, controls, and/or mechanisms.

Developer-provided training may be obtained from the developer or through the developer's documentation, videos, web-based resources, and other training materials.

Such systems may be unsupported due to the end of a product's service life, lack of availability of security updates, or lack of support for the operating system or application. Organizations using such systems accept a higher degree of risk relative to the use of supported products.

Organizations can use specialization to tailor system components to fit specific operational requirements, removing unnecessary capabilities that could be exploited by adversaries.

controls.title: Separation of System and User Functionality
controls.objective_name: SC-2: Separation of System and User Functionality
controls.statement: Separate user functionality, including user interface services, from system management functionality.
controls.discussion: System management functionality includes functions necessary to administer databases, network components, workstations, or servers, and typically requires privileged user access. The separation of user functionality from system management functionality is either physical or logical. Organizations implement separation of functionality as allowing only authorized administrators to access system management functionality and preventing users from accessing system management functionality.

controls.title: Security Function Isolation
controls.statement: Isolate security functions from nonsecurity functions.
controls.discussion: The establishment of security domains with clear boundaries that include the isolation of security functions from nonsecurity functions helps to create and maintain a trusted computing base for organizational systems. The isolation of security functions from nonsecurity functions includes, for example, trusted kernels and security perimeters. Trusted kernels only execute trusted code and trusted code only calls other trusted code.

controls.title: Information in Shared System Resources
controls.objective_name: SC-4: Information in Shared System Resources
controls.statement: Prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.
controls.discussion: The control of information in shared system resources (e.g., registers, cache memory, main memory, hard disks) is also commonly referred to as object reuse and residual information protection. This control prevents information, including encrypted representations of information, produced by the actions of prior users or roles (or the actions of processes acting on behalf of prior users or roles) from being available to any current users or roles (or current processes) that obtain access to shared system resources after those resources have been released back to systems.

controls.title: Denial-of-Service Protection

items.label: SC-5a: [Selection: Protect against; Limit] the effects of the following types of denial-of-service events: [Assignment: organization-defined types of denial-of-service events]; and
items.text: [Selection: Protect against; Limit] the effects of the following types of denial-of-service events: [Assignment: organization-defined types of denial-of-service events]; and

items.text: Employ the following controls to achieve the denial-of-service objective: [Assignment: organization-defined controls by type of denial-of-service event].

controls.discussion: Denial-of-service events may occur due to a variety of internal and external causes. Denial-of-service attacks can either be intentional (i.e., based on deliberate adversarial actions) or unintentional (e.g., due to an inadvertent triggering of a latent system vulnerability). Types of denial-of-service attacks include volumetric attacks, protocol attacks, and application-layer attacks. Volumetric attacks can overwhelm the processing capacity of systems.

controls.title: Resource Availability
controls.statement: Protect the availability of resources by allocating [Assignment: organization-defined resources] by [Assignment: organization-defined priority, quota, or other assignment strategy].
controls.discussion: Resource availability includes protecting against unauthorized resource consumption through the use of system quotas for storage and communications bandwidth.

controls.title: Boundary Protection

items.label: SC-7a: Monitor and control communications at the external managed interfaces to the system and at key internal managed interfaces within the system
items.text: Monitor and control communications at the external managed interfaces to the system and at key internal managed interfaces within the system

items.label: SC-7b: Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are [Selection: physically; logically] separated from internal organizational networks; and
items.text: Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are [Selection: physically; logically] separated from internal organizational networks; and

items.label: SC-7c: Connect to external networks or systems only through managed interfaces consisting of boundary protection devices arranged in accordance with an organizational security and privacy architecture.
items.text: Connect to external networks or systems only through managed interfaces consisting of boundary protection devices arranged in accordance with an organizational security and privacy architecture.

controls.discussion: Managed interfaces include gateways, routers, firewalls, guards, network-based malicious code analysis and virtualization systems, or encrypted tunnels implemented within a security architecture. Subnetworks that are physically or logically separated from internal networks are referred to as demilitarized zones or DMZs. Restricting or prohibiting interfaces within organizational systems includes restricting external web traffic to designated web servers within managed interfaces and prohibiting external traffic that appears to be spoofing internal addresses.

controls.title: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
controls.statement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to [Selection (one or more): prevent unauthorized disclosure of information; detect changes to information] during transmission.
controls.discussion: Protecting the confidentiality and integrity of transmitted information applies to internal and external networks as well as any system components that can transmit information including servers, notebook computers, desktop computers, mobile devices, printers, copiers, scanners, facsimile machines, and radios. Unprotected communication links can result in the disclosure or modification of information in transit. The use of cryptographic mechanisms to protect confidentiality and integrity during transmission is the primary means of implementing this control.

controls.title: Network Disconnect
controls.statement: Terminate the network connection associated with a communications session at the end of the session or after [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of inactivity.
controls.discussion: This control applies to both internal and external networks. Terminating connections associated with communications sessions include de-allocating associated TCP/IP address or port pairs at the operating system level, or de-allocating networking assignments at the application level if multiple application sessions are using a single operating system-level connection.

controls.title: Trusted Path

items.label: SC-11a: Provide a [Selection: physically; logically] isolated trusted communications path for communications between the user and the trusted components of the system; and
items.text: Provide a [Selection: physically; logically] isolated trusted communications path for communications between the user and the trusted components of the system; and

items.label: SC-11b: Permit users to invoke the trusted communications path for communications between the user and the following security functions of the system, including at a minimum, authentication and re-authentication: [Assignment: organization-defined security functions].
items.text: Permit users to invoke the trusted communications path for communications between the user and the following security functions of the system, including at a minimum, authentication and re-authentication: [Assignment: organization-defined security functions].

controls.discussion: Trusted paths are mechanisms by which users can communicate directly with security functions of systems with the requisite assurance to support information security and privacy policies. Trusted path mechanisms can be physical or logical. In physical trusted paths, the path from the user to the security function of the system consists of an unbroken physical chain of components that cannot be tampered with. Alternatively, in logical trusted paths, the path from the user to the security function of the system is protected by a trusted operating environment.

controls.title: Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management
controls.objective_name: SC-12: Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management
controls.statement: Establish and manage cryptographic keys when cryptography is employed within the system in accordance with the following key management requirements: [Assignment: organization-defined requirements for key generation, distribution, storage, access, and destruction].
controls.discussion: The requirements for cryptographic key management and establishment can be found in applicable federal laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. Cryptographic key management and establishment can employ either manual procedures or automated mechanisms with supporting manual procedures when automation is not feasible.

controls.title: Cryptographic Protection

items.label: SC-13a: Determine the [Assignment: organization-defined cryptographic uses]; and
items.text: Determine the [Assignment: organization-defined cryptographic uses]; and

items.label: SC-13b: Implement the following types of cryptography required for each specified cryptographic use: [Assignment: organization-defined types of cryptography for each specified cryptographic use].
items.text: Implement the following types of cryptography required for each specified cryptographic use: [Assignment: organization-defined types of cryptography for each specified cryptographic use].

controls.discussion: Cryptography can be employed to support a variety of security solutions including the protection of classified and controlled unclassified information, the provision of digital signatures, and the enforcement of information separation when authorized individuals have the clearance and formal access approvals for all information contained in cryptographically protected information. Cryptographic mechanisms used for the protection of information require the use of NIST-approved cryptographic algorithms and validated cryptographic modules.

controls.title: Collaborative Computing Devices and Applications
controls.objective_name: SC-15: Collaborative Computing Devices and Applications

items.label: SC-15a: Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and applications with the following exceptions: [Assignment: organization-defined exceptions where remote activation is to be allowed]; and
items.text: Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and applications with the following exceptions: [Assignment: organization-defined exceptions where remote activation is to be allowed]; and

items.label: SC-15b: Provide an explicit indication of use to users physically present at the devices.
items.text: Provide an explicit indication of use to users physically present at the devices.

controls.discussion: Prohibition or restriction of collaborative computing devices applies to information systems or system components prohibiting or restricting collaborative computing devices including audio or video conferencing devices, microphones, remote desktop software, and chat and messaging applications.

controls.title: Transmission of Security and Privacy Attributes
controls.objective_name: SC-16: Transmission of Security and Privacy Attributes
controls.statement: Associate [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy attributes] with information exchanged between systems and between system components.
controls.discussion: Security attributes can be explicitly or implicitly associated with the information contained in organizational systems or system components. Attributes are abstractions that represent the basic properties or characteristics of an entity with respect to safeguarding information. Security attributes are used to implement access control and flow control policies; reflect special dissemination, handling, or distribution instructions; or support other aspects of the information security policy.

controls.title: Public Key Infrastructure Certificates

items.label: SC-17a: Issue public key certificates under an [Assignment: organization-defined certificate policy] or obtain public key certificates from an approved service provider; and
items.text: Issue public key certificates under an [Assignment: organization-defined certificate policy] or obtain public key certificates from an approved service provider; and

items.label: SC-17b: Include only approved trust anchors in trust stores or certificate stores managed by the organization.
items.text: Include only approved trust anchors in trust stores or certificate stores managed by the organization.

controls.discussion: Public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates are digital certificates that bind the identity of a certificate holder to a public key with a digital signature. The certificate allows an entity presenting it to be authenticated as the holder of the private key corresponding to the public key in the certificate. Organizations are required to use PKI certificates that comply with X.509 standard.

controls.title: Mobile Code

items.label: SC-18a: Define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies; and
items.text: Define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies; and

items.label: SC-18b: Authorize, monitor, and control the use of mobile code within the system.
items.text: Authorize, monitor, and control the use of mobile code within the system.

controls.discussion: Mobile code technologies include Java, JavaScript, ActiveX, Postscript, PDF, Shockwave movies, Flash animations, and VBscript. Decisions regarding the employment of mobile code within organizational systems are based on the potential for the code to cause damage to the systems if used maliciously. Mobile code technologies can be allowed or prohibited based on their potential threat to the security of organizational systems.

controls.title: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Authoritative Source)
controls.objective_name: SC-20: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Authoritative Source)

items.label: SC-20a: Provide additional data origin authentication and integrity verification artifacts along with the authoritative name resolution data the system returns in response to external name/address resolution queries; and
items.text: Provide additional data origin authentication and integrity verification artifacts along with the authoritative name resolution data the system returns in response to external name/address resolution queries; and

items.label: SC-20b: Provide the means to indicate the security status of child zones and (if the child supports secure resolution services) to enable verification of a chain of trust among parent and child domains, when operating as part of a distributed, hierarchical namespace.
items.text: Provide the means to indicate the security status of child zones and (if the child supports secure resolution services) to enable verification of a chain of trust among parent and child domains, when operating as part of a distributed, hierarchical namespace.

controls.discussion: The Domain Name System (DNS) is a hierarchical and decentralized naming system for computers, services, or other resources connected to the internet or a private network. The Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) are a suite of extension specifications for securing data exchanged in the DNS. DNSSEC provides source authentication and data integrity for DNS lookups.

controls.title: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver)
controls.objective_name: SC-21: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver)
controls.statement: Request and perform data origin authentication and data integrity verification on the name/address resolution responses the system receives from authoritative sources.
controls.discussion: As a recursive or caching resolver, the system requests resolution of a query on behalf of a client and then stores (caches) the results. The results are then provided to clients requesting the same information. Organizations employ source authentication and data integrity verification mechanisms for DNS lookups to reduce susceptibility to attacks that manipulate DNS information (e.g., DNS cache poisoning).

controls.title: Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service
controls.objective_name: SC-22: Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service
controls.statement: Design, manage, and operate a collection of distributed name/address resolution services that together are fault-tolerant and implement internal/external role separation.
controls.discussion: The Domain Name System (DNS) implements a distributed, hierarchical naming system that allows users to use human-readable names to access internet resources. The integrity and availability of DNS services are critical to the operation of organizational systems. Organizations provide redundant and fault-tolerant DNS services to ensure availability.

controls.title: Session Authenticity
controls.statement: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions.
controls.discussion: Authenticity protection provides protection against man-in-the-middle attacks and session hijacking attempts. Security mechanisms used to protect message authenticity include transport layer security (TLS) and Secure Shell (SSH) protocol. Network address translation hides the real IP address of a system behind a router. Organizations can use network address translation as part of its defense-in-depth strategy.

controls.title: Fail in Known State
controls.statement: Fail to a [Assignment: organization-defined known system state] in the event of [Assignment: organization-defined types of system failures] preserving [Assignment: organization-defined system state information] in failure.
controls.discussion: Failure in a known state addresses security concerns in accordance with the mission and business needs of organizations. Failure in a known state can be used by organizations to secure information, prevent further compromise of a system, or facilitate recovery. The requirements for fail-safe states include preserving system state information in the event of a failure, transitioning to safe states as needed, and meeting specific security and privacy requirements.

controls.title: Thin Nodes
controls.statement: Employ minimal functionality and information storage on the following system components: [Assignment: organization-defined system components].
controls.discussion: The employment of thin nodes, such as diskless workstations or thin clients, reduces the attack surface of organizational systems by limiting the number of components that need to be protected and the types of attacks that can be successfully carried out against individual system components.

controls.title: Decoys
controls.statement: Include the following system components specifically selected to be the target of adversaries for detecting, deflecting, and analyzing such attempts: [Assignment: organization-defined system components].
controls.discussion: Decoys include systems and system components set up as honeypots to attract adversaries and detect and analyze adversary attacks. Honeypots are useful for detecting attacks before they damage production systems. Organizations ensure that decoys are realistic enough to attract adversaries but that the information gathered by adversaries during their interaction with the decoy is not sensitive.

controls.title: Platform-Independent Applications
controls.statement: Include within the system operating system-independent applications.
controls.discussion: Independence from operating system-specific mechanisms allows applications to run on a variety of operating systems, facilitating application portability, supporting contingency planning and continuity of operations, and facilitating disaster recovery and migration to new systems.

controls.title: Protection of Information at Rest
controls.objective_name: SC-28: Protection of Information at Rest
controls.statement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of the following information at rest on [Assignment: organization-defined system components or media]: [Assignment: organization-defined information].
controls.discussion: The confidentiality and integrity of information at rest is of concern in certain situations. Encryption is used to protect information at rest against unauthorized disclosure and modification. Encryption provides a means of protecting information from unauthorized access in the event of a physical security breach or loss of media. Organizations must balance the need for encryption with the performance requirements of the systems that process, store, and transmit information.

controls.title: Heterogeneity
controls.statement: Employ a diverse set of information technologies for the following system components in the implementation of the system: [Assignment: organization-defined system components].
controls.discussion: Increasing the diversity of systems reduces the likelihood that a single compromise or attack will affect all organizational systems. The use of heterogeneous operating systems, hardware, and firmware mitigates the risk that a single vulnerability in one type of system component can be exploited across all systems.

controls.title: Concealment and Misdirection
controls.statement: Employ the following concealment and misdirection techniques for [Assignment: organization-defined systems] at [Assignment: organization-defined time periods] to confuse and mislead adversaries: [Assignment: organization-defined concealment and misdirection techniques].
controls.discussion: Concealment and misdirection techniques involve placing information systems, or system components in locations that are hidden from adversaries and/or directing adversaries toward decoy systems, components, or locations rather than actual systems.

controls.title: Covert Channel Analysis

items.label: SC-31a: Perform a covert channel analysis to identify those aspects of communications within the system that are potential avenues for covert [Selection (one or more): storage; timing] channels; and
items.text: Perform a covert channel analysis to identify those aspects of communications within the system that are potential avenues for covert [Selection (one or more): storage; timing] channels; and

items.label: SC-31b: Estimate the maximum bandwidth of those channels.
items.text: Estimate the maximum bandwidth of those channels.

controls.discussion: Covert channels are paths that can be used to transfer information in a manner that violates the system's security policy. Covert channel analysis is performed to identify those aspects of communications within the system that are not intended to transfer information but could be used for that purpose.

controls.title: System Partitioning
controls.statement: Partition the system into [Assignment: organization-defined system components] residing in separate [Selection: physical; logical] domains or environments based on [Assignment: organization-defined circumstances for physical or logical separation of components].
controls.discussion: System partitioning is a part of a defense-in-depth protection strategy. Organizations determine the degree to which partitioning is needed based on assessments of risk. Physical separation of system components can reduce the impact of a security breach to one component since damage does not automatically propagate to other components in a different physical environment.

controls.title: Non-Modifiable Executable Programs

items.label: SC-34a: The operating environment from hardware-enforced, read-only media; and
items.text: The operating environment from hardware-enforced, read-only media; and

items.label: SC-34b: The following applications from hardware-enforced, read-only media: [Assignment: organization-defined applications].
items.text: The following applications from hardware-enforced, read-only media: [Assignment: organization-defined applications].

controls.discussion: Non-modifiable executable programs include Commercial Off The Shelf (COTS) firmware and operating systems. Organizations employ trusted boot procedures to ensure that only authorized code is loaded during the startup process. Hardware roots of trust provide organizations with strong assurance that only authorized code is loaded.

controls.title: External Malicious Code Identification
controls.statement: Include system components that detect malicious code or malware in the execution environment and activate the following response: [Assignment: organization-defined response].
controls.discussion: A detonation chamber, also known as a sandbox or dynamic analysis environment, is a mechanism that provides an isolated, instrumented environment for the safe execution of potentially malicious code. Suspicious or unknown software is executed in the detonation chamber to observe its behavior and to provide indicators of compromise or attack.

controls.title: Distributed Processing and Storage
controls.statement: Distribute the following processing and storage components across multiple [Selection: physical; logical] domains or environments: [Assignment: organization-defined processing and storage components].
controls.discussion: Distributing processing and storage across multiple physical locations creates resiliency against adversarial attacks that target a single data center or geographic location. Multiple processing and storage sites also support mission/business continuity and disaster recovery.

controls.title: Out-of-Band Channels
controls.statement: Employ [Assignment: organization-defined out-of-band channels] for the physical delivery or electronic transmission of [Assignment: organization-defined information, system components, or devices] to [Assignment: organization-defined individuals or systems].
controls.discussion: Out-of-band channels include local non-network (e.g., air-gapped) connections, personal delivery, US Postal Service or express delivery services, and encrypted (e.g., Secure Shell [SSH] or Transport Layer Security [TLS]) virtual private networks (VPNs). Out-of-band channels are used for the exchange of sensitive information, such as initial credentials, and for the transmission of trusted software.

controls.title: Operations Security
controls.statement: Employ the following operations security controls to protect key organizational information throughout the system development life cycle: [Assignment: organization-defined operations security controls].
controls.discussion: Operations security (OPSEC) is the process of protecting individual pieces of data that could be grouped together to give the bigger picture (called aggregation). Organizations use OPSEC to identify, analyze, and control information associated with system operations that could be used by adversaries to disrupt or compromise organizational operations.

controls.title: Process Isolation
controls.statement: Maintain a separate execution domain for each executing process.
controls.discussion: Systems can maintain separate execution domains for each executing process by assigning each process a separate address space. Each system process has a distinct address space so that communication between processes is performed in a manner controlled through the security functions, and one process cannot modify the executing code of another process.

controls.title: Wireless Link Protection
controls.statement: Protect external and internal [Assignment: organization-defined wireless links] from the following signal parameter attacks: [Assignment: organization-defined types of signal parameter attacks or references to sources for such attacks].
controls.discussion: Wireless link protection applies to both internal and external wireless communication links and includes the use of cryptographic mechanisms, jamming-resistant communications protocols, access point configurations, and other technical or procedural measures to protect wireless links from signal parameter attacks.

controls.title: Port and I/O Device Access
controls.objective_name: SC-41: Port and I/O Device Access
controls.statement: Enforce physical and logical access restrictions to [Assignment: organization-defined connection ports or input/output devices] on the following systems or system components: [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components].
controls.discussion: This control addresses the physical and logical access to ports and I/O devices to prevent unauthorized access, whether from unauthorized physical users or from malicious software or code that could use the I/O device as a vector for compromise or data exfiltration.

controls.title: Sensor Capability and Data

items.label: SC-42a: Prohibit [Selection (one or more): the use of devices possessing [Assignment: organization-defined environmental sensing capabilities] in [Assignment: organization-defined facilities, areas, or systems]; the remote activation of environmental sensing capabilities on organizational systems or system components with the following exceptions: [Assignment: organization-defined exceptions where remote activation of sensors is allowed]]; and
items.text: Prohibit [Selection (one or more): the use of devices possessing [Assignment: organization-defined environmental sensing capabilities] in [Assignment: organization-defined facilities, areas, or systems]; the remote activation of environmental sensing capabilities on organizational systems or system components with the following exceptions: [Assignment: organization-defined exceptions where remote activation of sensors is allowed]]; and

items.label: SC-42b: Provide an explicit indication of sensor use to [Assignment: organization-defined group of users].
items.text: Provide an explicit indication of sensor use to [Assignment: organization-defined group of users].

controls.discussion: Sensors can include GPS sensors, cameras, microphones, and other sensor technologies embedded in systems or system components. Organizations take appropriate steps to disable or limit the use of sensors when they are not needed for authorized system functions or when they might pose a risk to the privacy of individuals.

controls.title: Usage Restrictions

items.label: SC-43a: Establish usage restrictions and implementation guidelines for the following system components: [Assignment: organization-defined system components]; and
items.text: Establish usage restrictions and implementation guidelines for the following system components: [Assignment: organization-defined system components]; and

items.label: SC-43b: Authorize, monitor, and control the use of such components within the system.
items.text: Authorize, monitor, and control the use of such components within the system.

controls.discussion: Usage restrictions include prohibiting or restricting the use of shared systems resources that could result in unauthorized information disclosure and protecting information provided to vendors or manufacturers for service or repair.

controls.title: Detonation Chambers
controls.statement: Employ a detonation chamber capability within [Assignment: organization-defined system, system component, or location].
controls.discussion: A detonation chamber is a contained environment in which organizations execute malicious code and analyze the behavior of the malicious code. Detonation chambers are used by organizations to understand the full capability and intent of malicious code before it can affect their systems.

controls.title: System Time Synchronization
controls.statement: Synchronize system clocks within and between systems and system components.
controls.discussion: Time stamps for digital records are critical to the integrity of audit trails and other records. Synchronization of internal system clocks is important to ensure that time stamps are consistent across organizational systems. Organizations use network time protocols to synchronize clocks and to maintain time stamp integrity.

controls.title: Cross Domain Policy Enforcement
controls.statement: Implement a hardware-enforced separation of [Assignment: organization-defined domains] using [Assignment: organization-defined cross domain policy enforcement mechanism].
controls.discussion: Cross-domain policy enforcement mechanisms enforce information flow policies at designated cross-domain boundaries. These mechanisms operate as information flow guardians for specified types of information and ensure that only authorized information flows between different security domains.

controls.title: Alternate Communications Paths
controls.statement: Maintain [Assignment: organization-defined alternative communications paths] to support essential mission and business functions.
controls.discussion: Organizations use alternate communications paths to support continuity of communications for essential organizational missions and business functions. Alternate communications paths are separate and independent from primary communications paths to avoid single points of failure.

controls.title: Sensor Relocation
controls.statement: Relocate [Assignment: organization-defined system components] to other locations in response to [Assignment: organization-defined conditions or cyber incidents].
controls.discussion: Sensor relocation involves moving or changing the locations of sensors and other monitoring devices in response to changing threats or conditions. This can help organizations maintain situational awareness and avoid having adversaries learn the locations and capabilities of organizational sensing and monitoring infrastructure.

controls.title: Hardware-Enforced Separation and Policy Enforcement
controls.objective_name: SC-49: Hardware-Enforced Separation and Policy Enforcement
controls.statement: Implement hardware-enforced [Assignment: organization-defined separation and policy enforcement mechanisms] between [Assignment: organization-defined domains].
controls.discussion: Hardware-enforced separation and policy enforcement mechanisms are implemented at the hardware level and are more difficult for adversaries to circumvent than software-based mechanisms. Hardware mechanisms can separate different security domains and enforce security policies even when software on the system is compromised.

controls.title: Software-Enforced Separation and Policy Enforcement
controls.objective_name: SC-50: Software-Enforced Separation and Policy Enforcement
controls.statement: Implement software-enforced [Assignment: organization-defined separation and policy enforcement mechanisms] between [Assignment: organization-defined domains].
controls.discussion: Software-enforced separation and policy enforcement mechanisms are implemented in the operating system or application software. While typically less robust than hardware enforcement mechanisms, software-enforced mechanisms are often less expensive to implement and can be effective when used in conjunction with other controls.

controls.title: Hardware-Based Protection

items.label: SC-51a: Employ hardware-based, write-protect for [Assignment: organization-defined system firmware components]; and
items.text: Employ hardware-based, write-protect for [Assignment: organization-defined system firmware components]; and

items.label: SC-51b: Implement specific procedures for [Assignment: organization-defined authorized individuals] to manually disable hardware write-protect for firmware modifications and re-enable the write-protect prior to returning to operational mode.
items.text: Implement specific procedures for [Assignment: organization-defined authorized individuals] to manually disable hardware write-protect for firmware modifications and re-enable the write-protect prior to returning to operational mode.

controls.discussion: Organizations employ hardware-based security mechanisms in addition to software-based mechanisms. Hardware-based security mechanisms include hardware memory protection, hardware-based virtualization, and trusted platform modules (TPM) to provide stronger security guarantees.

Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the system and information integrity policy and the associated system and information integrity controls
items.text: Develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]: 1. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the system and information integrity policy and the associated system and information integrity controls

items.text: Designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the system and information integrity policy and procedures; and

items.label: SI-1c: Review and update the current system and information integrity: 1. Policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]; and 2. Procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].
items.text: Review and update the current system and information integrity: 1. Policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]; and 2. Procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].

controls.discussion: This control addresses the establishment of policy and procedures for the effective implementation of selected security controls and control enhancements in the SI family. Policy and procedures reflect applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

controls.title: Flaw Remediation

items.label: SI-2a: Identify, report, and correct system flaws
items.text: Identify, report, and correct system flaws

items.label: SI-2b: Test software and firmware updates related to flaw remediation for effectiveness and potential side effects before installation
items.text: Test software and firmware updates related to flaw remediation for effectiveness and potential side effects before installation

items.label: SI-2c: Install security-relevant software and firmware updates within [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of the release of the updates; and
items.text: Install security-relevant software and firmware updates within [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of the release of the updates; and

items.label: SI-2d: Incorporate flaw remediation into the organizational configuration management process.
items.text: Incorporate flaw remediation into the organizational configuration management process.

controls.discussion: The intent of this control is to identify, report, and correct information system flaws and to test software and firmware updates related to flaw remediation for effectiveness and potential side effects before installation. Organizations identify systems affected by announced software vulnerabilities and take action in accordance with a prescribed risk-based decision process, applying patches, service packs, hot fixes, or other mitigations depending on the vulnerability and the organization's risk tolerance.

controls.title: Malicious Code Protection

items.label: SI-3a: Implement [Selection (one or more): signature based; non-signature based] malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code
items.text: Implement [Selection (one or more): signature based; non-signature based] malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code

items.label: SI-3b: Automatically update malicious code protection mechanisms as new releases are available in accordance with organizational configuration management policy and procedures
items.text: Automatically update malicious code protection mechanisms as new releases are available in accordance with organizational configuration management policy and procedures

Perform periodic scans of the system [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and real-time scans of files from external sources at [Selection (one or more): endpoint; network entry and exit points] as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed in accordance with organizational policy; and 2. [Selection (one or more): block malicious code; quarantine malicious code; take [Assignment: organization-defined action]]; and send alert to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] in response to malicious code detection; and
items.text: Configure malicious code protection mechanisms to: 1. Perform periodic scans of the system [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and real-time scans of files from external sources at [Selection (one or more): endpoint; network entry and exit points] as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed in accordance with organizational policy; and 2. [Selection (one or more): block malicious code; quarantine malicious code; take [Assignment: organization-defined action]]; and send alert to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] in response to malicious code detection; and

items.label: SI-3d: Address the receipt of false positives during malicious code detection and eradication and the resulting potential impact on the availability of the system.
items.text: Address the receipt of false positives during malicious code detection and eradication and the resulting potential impact on the availability of the system.

controls.discussion: Malicious code includes viruses, worms, Trojan horses, and spyware. Malicious code can be encoded in various formats (e.g., UUENCODE, Unicode), contained within compressed or hidden files, or hidden in files using techniques such as steganography. Organizations require malicious code protection mechanisms to be used at entry and exit points in the system, on system components, and on workstations and servers.

controls.title: System Monitoring

items.text: Monitor the system to detect: 1. Attacks and indicators of potential attacks in accordance with the following monitoring objectives: [Assignment: organization-defined monitoring objectives]; and 2. Unauthorized local, network, and remote connections

items.text: Identify unauthorized use of the system through the following techniques and methods: [Assignment: organization-defined techniques and methods]

items.text: Invoke internal monitoring capabilities or deploy monitoring devices: 1. Strategically within the system to collect organization-determined essential information; and 2. At ad hoc locations within the system to track specific types of transactions of interest to the organization

items.text: Analyze detected events and anomalies

items.text: Adjust the level of system monitoring activity when there is a change in risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation
