items.text: Provide [Assignment: organization-defined system monitoring information] to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] [Selection (one or more): as needed; [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]].

controls.discussion: System monitoring includes external and internal monitoring. External monitoring includes the observation of events occurring at the system boundary (e.g., part of perimeter defense and target environment preparation). Internal monitoring includes the observation of events occurring within the system. Organizations analyze monitoring information using security information and event management (SIEM) tools or other analytical capabilities.

controls.title: Security Alerts, Advisories, and Directives
controls.objective_name: SI-5: Security Alerts, Advisories, and Directives

items.label: SI-5a: Receive system security alerts, advisories, and directives from [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations] on an ongoing basis
items.text: Receive system security alerts, advisories, and directives from [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations] on an ongoing basis

items.label: SI-5b: Generate internal security alerts, advisories, and directives as deemed necessary
items.text: Generate internal security alerts, advisories, and directives as deemed necessary

items.label: SI-5c: Disseminate security alerts, advisories, and directives to: [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]; [Assignment: organization-defined elements within the organization]; [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations]]; and
items.text: Disseminate security alerts, advisories, and directives to: [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]; [Assignment: organization-defined elements within the organization]; [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations]]; and

items.label: SI-5d: Implement security directives in accordance with established time frames, or notify the issuing organization of the degree of noncompliance.
items.text: Implement security directives in accordance with established time frames, or notify the issuing organization of the degree of noncompliance.

controls.discussion: Security alerts, advisories, and directives are generated by organizations and disseminated to appropriate organizational elements such as chief information officers, system owners, authorizing officials, information system security officers, and mission/business owners. Organizations receive security alerts, advisories, and directives from established sources such as the Department of Homeland Security.

controls.title: Security and Privacy Function Verification
controls.objective_name: SI-6: Security and Privacy Function Verification

items.label: SI-6a: Verify the correct operation of [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy functions]
items.text: Verify the correct operation of [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy functions]

items.label: SI-6b: Perform the verification of the functions specified in SI-6a [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined system transitional states]; upon command by user with appropriate privilege; [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]]
items.text: Perform the verification of the functions specified in SI-6a [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined system transitional states]; upon command by user with appropriate privilege; [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]]

items.label: SI-6c: Alert [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] to failed security and privacy verification tests; and
items.text: Alert [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] to failed security and privacy verification tests; and

items.label: SI-6d: [Selection (one or more): Shut the system down; Restart the system; [Assignment: organization-defined alternative action(s)]] when anomalies are discovered.
items.text: [Selection (one or more): Shut the system down; Restart the system; [Assignment: organization-defined alternative action(s)]] when anomalies are discovered.

controls.discussion: Security verification checking is a form of integrity checking applied to security functions. Organizations use this control to verify that the security functions of systems operate correctly and to verify the security state of systems. Verification checks are executed as a normal part of system operation.

controls.title: Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity
controls.objective_name: SI-7: Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity

items.label: SI-7a: Employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to the following software, firmware, and information: [Assignment: organization-defined software, firmware, and information]; and
items.text: Employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to the following software, firmware, and information: [Assignment: organization-defined software, firmware, and information]; and

items.label: SI-7b: Take the following actions when unauthorized changes to the software, firmware, and information are detected: [Assignment: organization-defined actions].
items.text: Take the following actions when unauthorized changes to the software, firmware, and information are detected: [Assignment: organization-defined actions].

controls.discussion: Unauthorized changes to software, firmware, and information can occur due to errors or malicious activity (sabotage). Software, firmware, and information integrity checks are performed at startup or by continuous monitoring tools, intrusion detection systems, and malware detection. The use of cryptographic mechanisms such as digital signatures and hash functions to detect unauthorized changes helps to ensure the integrity of critical organizational systems, software, firmware, and information.

controls.title: Spam Protection

items.label: SI-8a: Employ spam protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and act on unsolicited messages; and
items.text: Employ spam protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and act on unsolicited messages; and

items.label: SI-8b: Update spam protection mechanisms when new releases are available in accordance with organizational configuration management policy and procedures.
items.text: Update spam protection mechanisms when new releases are available in accordance with organizational configuration management policy and procedures.

controls.discussion: An anti-spamming policy and the use of spam protection mechanisms address the problem of spam being used as a vector for delivering malicious code. Organizations consider spam as not just a nuisance but also as a potential security threat due to its use as a delivery vehicle for phishing attacks and malware.

controls.title: Information Input Validation
controls.statement: Check the validity of the following information inputs: [Assignment: organization-defined information inputs to the system].
controls.discussion: Checking the validity of information inputs ensures that information entered into systems meets specific requirements and that the system will not accept data values that are outside of the expected parameters. Invalid inputs may result in incorrect output or compromised security.

controls.title: Error Handling

items.label: SI-11a: Generate error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited; and
items.text: Generate error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited; and

items.label: SI-11b: Reveal error messages only to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].
items.text: Reveal error messages only to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].

controls.discussion: The structure and content of error messages are carefully considered by organizations. Error messages should generate useful information for users but should not generate information that could be exploited by adversaries. Sanitized error messages that do not include information that could be used to compromise systems are important for protecting organizational information.

controls.title: Information Management and Retention
controls.statement: Manage and retain information within the system and information output from the system in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, guidelines, and operational requirements.
controls.discussion: Information management and retention involves the management of information throughout its life cycle, including collection, use, storage, dissemination, and ultimate disposition. Organizations identify applicable laws and regulations addressing retention of organizational information and ensure that systems are capable of retaining information in accordance with those laws and regulations.

controls.title: Predictable Failure Prevention

items.label: SI-13a: Determine mean time to failure (MTTF) for the following system components in specific environments of operation: [Assignment: organization-defined system components]; and
items.text: Determine mean time to failure (MTTF) for the following system components in specific environments of operation: [Assignment: organization-defined system components]; and

items.label: SI-13b: Provide substitute system components and a means to exchange active and standby components in accordance with the following criteria: [Assignment: organization-defined MTTF substitution criteria].
items.text: Provide substitute system components and a means to exchange active and standby components in accordance with the following criteria: [Assignment: organization-defined MTTF substitution criteria].

controls.discussion: Predictable failure prevention can be achieved through redundancy, providing multiple instances of system components that perform the same function, and load balancing, distributing work among multiple system components. Organizations consider the potential for predictable failures in determining the types of redundancy to provide.

controls.title: Non-Persistence
controls.statement: Implement non-persistent [Assignment: organization-defined system components and services] that are initiated in a clean, known state and terminated [Assignment: organization-defined conditions, events, or time period].
controls.discussion: Non-persistence applies to designated system components and services. Non-persistent operational environments include temporary desktops, temporary virtual machines, and reimage-on-use techniques that ensure systems start from known states. This control is valuable when organizations are concerned about the persistent presence of malicious code following an incident.

controls.title: Information Output Filtering
controls.statement: Validate information outputs from the following software programs and/or applications to ensure that the information is consistent with the expected content: [Assignment: organization-defined software programs and/or applications].
controls.discussion: Information output filtering focuses on the content of the output rather than the format of the output. Information output filtering may be particularly important for the outputs of web-based applications. Output filtering helps to prevent data injection attacks and other types of attacks that use output mechanisms as attack vectors.

controls.title: Memory Protection
controls.statement: Implement the following controls to protect the system memory from unauthorized code execution: [Assignment: organization-defined controls].
controls.discussion: Memory protection mechanisms include data execution prevention and address space layout randomization. Data execution prevention ensures that only certain regions of memory are executable. Address space layout randomization makes it harder for adversaries to exploit memory vulnerabilities because memory addresses are randomized.

controls.title: Fail-Safe Procedures
controls.statement: Implement the indicated fail-safe procedures when the indicated failures occur: [Assignment: organization-defined list of failure conditions and associated fail-safe procedures].
controls.discussion: Fail-safe procedures reflect organizational policies and operational requirements for actions to be taken when specified failure conditions occur. Fail-safe procedures can help organizations avoid unsafe conditions as a result of failures. Fail-safe procedures include transitioning systems to predefined safe states when specific failures occur.

controls.title: Personally Identifiable Information Quality Operations
controls.objective_name: SI-18: Personally Identifiable Information Quality Operations

items.label: SI-18a: Check the accuracy, relevance, timeliness, and completeness of personally identifiable information across the information life cycle [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; and
items.text: Check the accuracy, relevance, timeliness, and completeness of personally identifiable information across the information life cycle [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; and

items.label: SI-18b: Correct or delete inaccurate or outdated personally identifiable information.
items.text: Correct or delete inaccurate or outdated personally identifiable information.

controls.discussion: De-identification is a process of removing information that can be used to identify specific individuals from datasets. Organizations use de-identification techniques to protect privacy while still retaining the usefulness of data for analytical purposes. De-identification techniques include generalization, suppression, noise addition, permutation, pseudonymization, and aggregation.

controls.title: De-Identification

items.label: SI-19a: Remove the following elements of personally identifiable information from datasets: [Assignment: organization-defined elements of personally identifiable information]; and
items.text: Remove the following elements of personally identifiable information from datasets: [Assignment: organization-defined elements of personally identifiable information]; and

items.label: SI-19b: Evaluate [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] for effectiveness of de-identification.
items.text: Evaluate [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] for effectiveness of de-identification.

controls.discussion: Re-identification is the process of matching de-identified records with individuals. Organizations may use re-identification as part of data management or program evaluation while protecting individuals' privacy through limited access controls and other restrictions.

controls.title: Tainting
controls.statement: Employ the following techniques to embed data tainting in the organizational systems: [Assignment: organization-defined tainting techniques].
controls.discussion: Data tainting allows organizations to track information as it flows through systems and to detect potential unauthorized disclosures. Tagged data can be tracked as it is copied or transmitted through the system, enabling organizations to determine if sensitive data is being improperly accessed or exfiltrated.

controls.title: Information Refresh
controls.statement: Refresh [Assignment: organization-defined information] at [Assignment: organization-defined frequencies] from trusted sources to implement refresh.
controls.discussion: Information refresh involves periodically replacing information held in systems with updated data from trusted sources. This helps to ensure that stale or potentially compromised information does not persist in systems longer than necessary.

controls.title: Information Diversity

items.label: SI-22a: Identify the following alternative sources of information for [Assignment: organization-defined essential functions and services]: [Assignment: organization-defined alternative information sources]; and
items.text: Identify the following alternative sources of information for [Assignment: organization-defined essential functions and services]: [Assignment: organization-defined alternative information sources]; and

items.label: SI-22b: Use an alternative information source for the execution of essential functions or services on [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components] when the primary source of information is corrupted or unavailable.
items.text: Use an alternative information source for the execution of essential functions or services on [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components] when the primary source of information is corrupted or unavailable.

controls.discussion: Organizations take steps to protect the most critical system resources, such as trusted kernels and system boot images, to prevent adversaries from modifying these resources in ways that could compromise the integrity of systems. Read-only media, write protection, and cryptographic verification mechanisms are used to protect critical resources.

controls.title: Information Fragmentation

items.label: SI-23a: Fragment the following information: [Assignment: organization-defined information]; and
items.text: Fragment the following information: [Assignment: organization-defined information]; and

items.label: SI-23b: Distribute the fragmented information across the following systems or system components: [Assignment organization-defined systems or system components].
items.text: Distribute the fragmented information across the following systems or system components: [Assignment organization-defined systems or system components].

controls.discussion: Information integrity verification involves the use of mechanisms such as checksums and hash functions to verify that information has not been modified or corrupted. Organizations use information integrity verification to detect unauthorized modifications to information in storage or in transit.

Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the supply chain risk management policy and the associated supply chain risk management controls

Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the supply chain risk management policy and the associated supply chain risk management controls

items.text: Designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the supply chain risk management policy and procedures; and

items.text: Review and update the current supply chain risk management: 1. Policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]; and 2. Procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].

controls.discussion: This control addresses the establishment of policy and procedures for the effective implementation of selected security controls and control enhancements in the SR family. Policy and procedures reflect applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

controls.title: Supply Chain Risk Management Plan
controls.objective_name: SR-2: Supply Chain Risk Management Plan

items.label: SR-2a: Develop a plan for managing supply chain risks associated with the research and development, design, manufacturing, acquisition, delivery, integration, operations and maintenance, and disposal of the following systems, system components or system services: [Assignment: organization-defined systems, system components, or system services]
items.text: Develop a plan for managing supply chain risks associated with the research and development, design, manufacturing, acquisition, delivery, integration, operations and maintenance, and disposal of the following systems, system components or system services: [Assignment: organization-defined systems, system components, or system services]

items.label: SR-2b: Review and update the supply chain risk management plan [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] or as required, to address threat, organizational or environmental changes; and
items.text: Review and update the supply chain risk management plan [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] or as required, to address threat, organizational or environmental changes; and

items.label: SR-2c: Protect the supply chain risk management plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification.
items.text: Protect the supply chain risk management plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

controls.discussion: Organizations develop supply chain risk management (SCRM) plans to address the risks associated with the acquisition, use, and management of information technology products and services. Supply chain risk management plans are developed as part of the overall organizational risk management program and support the information security and privacy programs.

controls.title: Supply Chain Controls and Processes
controls.objective_name: SR-3: Supply Chain Controls and Processes

items.label: SR-3a: Establish a process or processes to identify and address weaknesses or deficiencies in the supply chain elements and processes of [Assignment: organization-defined system or system component] in coordination with [Assignment: organization-defined supply chain personnel]
items.text: Establish a process or processes to identify and address weaknesses or deficiencies in the supply chain elements and processes of [Assignment: organization-defined system or system component] in coordination with [Assignment: organization-defined supply chain personnel]

items.label: SR-3b: Employ the following controls to protect against supply chain risks to the system, system component, or system service and to limit the harm or consequences from supply chainrelated events: [Assignment: organization-defined supply chain controls]; and
items.text: Employ the following controls to protect against supply chain risks to the system, system component, or system service and to limit the harm or consequences from supply chainrelated events: [Assignment: organization-defined supply chain controls]; and

items.label: SR-3c: Document the selected and implemented supply chain processes and controls in [Selection: security and privacy plans; supply chain risk management plan; [Assignment: organization-defined document]].
items.text: Document the selected and implemented supply chain processes and controls in [Selection: security and privacy plans; supply chain risk management plan; [Assignment: organization-defined document]].

controls.discussion: Supply chain risk management controls help organizations reduce the risk of adversarial attacks by identifying and addressing threats at each stage of the supply chain. This includes threats from external and internal sources. Supply chain controls supplement the information security measures organizations employ to protect systems and components.

controls.title: Provenance
controls.statement: Document, monitor, and maintain valid provenance of the following systems, system components, and associated data: [Assignment: organization-defined systems, system components, and associated data].
controls.discussion: The provenance of systems, system components, and associated data is important for understanding the origin of these items and the chain of custody. Provenance information helps organizations assess the risk associated with using these items and determine whether they have been subject to tampering.

controls.title: Acquisition Strategies, Tools, and Methods
controls.objective_name: SR-5: Acquisition Strategies, Tools, and Methods
controls.statement: Employ the following acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods to protect against, identify, and mitigate supply chain risks: [Assignment: organization-defined acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods].
controls.discussion: Acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods are used to protect against supply chain risks. Organizations use these mechanisms to ensure that suppliers and third-party service providers implement appropriate security measures and that products and services meet security requirements.

controls.title: Supplier Assessments and Reviews
controls.statement: Assess suppliers and third-party providers of [Assignment: organization-defined supply chain elements, processes, and services] using [Assignment: organization-defined assessment methods and procedures].
controls.discussion: Third-party providers of supply chain elements present risks because organizations typically have less control over external providers than over internal operations. Assessing suppliers and third-party providers involves evaluating their security practices, contractual obligations, and performance.

controls.title: Supply Chain Operations Security
controls.statement: Employ the following Operations Security (OPSEC) controls to protect supply chain-related information for the system, system component, or system service: [Assignment: organization-defined Operations Security (OPSEC) controls].
controls.discussion: Operations Security (OPSEC) practices help organizations protect supply chain information from adversaries who might use that information to target specific supply chain elements. OPSEC controls include restrictions on the sharing of information about the supply chain.

controls.title: Notification Agreements
controls.statement: Establish agreements and procedures with entities involved in the supply chain for the system, system component, or system service for the [Assignment: organization-defined supply chain agreement contents] notification.
controls.discussion: Notification agreements ensure that organizations are informed about significant events related to the supply chain, such as security breaches, vulnerabilities in products, or disruptions to services. These agreements enable organizations to take timely action in response to supply chain events.

controls.title: Tamper Resistance and Detection
controls.statement: Implement a tamper protection program for the system, system component, or system service.
controls.discussion: Tamper resistance and detection involves the use of physical and logical mechanisms to prevent, detect, and respond to unauthorized modifications to hardware and software during the supply chain process. Organizations use tamper-evident packaging, seals, and other mechanisms to detect tampering.

controls.title: Inspection of Systems or Components
controls.objective_name: SR-10: Inspection of Systems or Components
controls.statement: Inspect the following systems or system components [Selection (one or more): at random; at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; upon [Assignment: organization-defined indications of need for inspection]] to detect tampering: [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components].
controls.discussion: Inspecting systems and system components for tampering allows organizations to detect supply chain compromises before affected components are deployed into operational environments. Inspections can include physical examinations, functional testing, and other techniques to verify the integrity of components.

controls.title: Component Authenticity

items.label: SR-11a: Develop and implement anti-counterfeit policy and procedures that include the means to detect and prevent counterfeit components from entering the system; and
items.text: Develop and implement anti-counterfeit policy and procedures that include the means to detect and prevent counterfeit components from entering the system; and

items.label: SR-11b: Report counterfeit system components to [Selection (one or more): source of counterfeit component; [Assignment: organization-defined external reporting organizations]; [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]].
items.text: Report counterfeit system components to [Selection (one or more): source of counterfeit component; [Assignment: organization-defined external reporting organizations]; [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]].

controls.discussion: Component authenticity involves verifying that system components are genuine products from trusted suppliers, as opposed to counterfeit products. Counterfeit components may lack the security properties of genuine components and may contain malicious code or vulnerabilities.

controls.title: Component Disposal
controls.statement: Dispose of, destroy, or repurpose system components using [Assignment: organization-defined techniques and methods].
controls.discussion: Disposing, destroying, or repurposing system components must be done in a manner that ensures that sensitive information contained in the components is not disclosed and that the components cannot be returned to service without proper sanitization. Organizations use component disposal procedures to ensure that components are decommissioned in a secure manner.
